scope: Optional 87-class native detector integration and explicit host ROI fusion; same-model TensorRT FP32 controls

upstream.checkpoint_origin: Tracked checkpoint provided by upstream; not a newly exported deployment engine

environment.dependency_boundary: Nested export environment reuses the base native packages; standard separate web/inference virtual-environment launcher was not exercised

applied.implementation: Expose existing exact host depth ROI medians in native PRF2 load_detector through startup-frozen PRS_DEPTH_FUSION; one full aligned FP32 plane transfer replaces repeated per-object GPU reductions
applied.scope: Same-frame distance mode A only; geometry and temporal-depth plus host fail explicitly
applied.optional_walk_selection: PRS_DETECTION_MODEL=yolo26n-walk; original HF acceleration plan does not qualify these weights
other_changes: Freeze selected detector/manifest before hello and lazy load; health uses the selected weights
Preserve independent HF, local PRF2 and resident-v1 admission contracts; walk is admitted only by the local client contract
Validate actual walk thresholds and neutral merged pedestrian-light output in service probes
Add shared registry to remote deployment allowlists and optional manifest to phone test bundle; no remote deployment performed

protocol.sequence: GPU fusion before, host fusion, GPU fusion after; separate fresh processes; all runs use identical TensorRT depth artifacts
protocol.timing: First frame and load are separate; every remaining frame is retained in the steady distribution; no clipping, subsampling or outlier deletion
protocol.input: All source frames in original order with source index/fps timestamps; RGB PIL bilinear maximum edge 640 and JPEG80; SDK depth edge 768 batch1 FP32, TF32 disabled
protocol.steady_video_metric: server_ms is complete native inference host duration including detection, depth, fusion transfer/reduction, tracking, risk and rendering; depth_fusion_ms is a nested phase, not depth Forward
protocol.validation: Complete aligned FP32 map comparison/cache I/O occurs after the timed prediction; all object fields, raw detections and rendered JPEG are compared exactly
protocol.unchanged: Within each group: checkpoint, source, engine, thresholds, ROI, pedestrian-light rules, risk, timestamps, precision and depth frequency; never infer acceleration across the two model weights
protocol.shared_host: Ordinary Windows workstation, no concurrent benchmark GPU jobs; CPU scheduling and thermal/clock drift were not controlled. Short CPU-only client checks occurred during the initial sequence
protocol.replicate_reason: Initial walk-night host mean was 0.595% slower than its first control and 7.019% faster than its second control. Run one additional complete GPU/host/GPU sequence with unchanged inputs and independent baseline/cache; retain both sequences, including the regression. This is an explicit diagnostic replication, not replacement or filtering.

reproduction.before: python -B -m tools.benchmark_depth_integration --video model_tests/datasets/street-video/mot17/MOT17-{07|10}-FRCNN-raw.mp4 --detection-model {model} --backend tensorrt --fusion gpu --manifest models/experiments/depth-serving-fp32/manifest.json --depth-cache models/experiments/{fresh-cache} --output benchmarks/{fresh-before}
reproduction.candidate: Use the same command with --fusion host, a new --output and --reference benchmarks/{fresh-before}
reproduction.after: Use the same command with --fusion gpu, another new --output and --reference benchmarks/{fresh-before}
reproduction.replicate: Use an independent fresh cache and three new report directories with identical model/video/settings; no automatic retries
reproduction.service: python -B -m tools.check_local_mvp --frames 31 --output {new-service-report}; selected model/fusion must match worker environment
reproduction.signal: Use --frames 1 --input models/experiments/walk-fusion-inputs/mot07-signal-frame286.png with the same service probe; extract original frame286 and require the JPEG fixture hash in signal-fixture.json

output_consistency.scope: Host fusion and after-controls versus the same-model TensorRT GPU-fusion reference, including cold frames
output_consistency.limitation: This does not assert TensorRT versus Torch bitwise equality; previously reported small FP32 differences remain in ../../2026-10-26/depth-integration/summary.json
output_consistency.new_classes: Only neutral pedestrian light appeared among classes 80-86 in these clips; pole, bollard, traffic_cone and stairs have no positive full-video evidence here

real_service.protocol: PRF2 through actual Web 8766 and native worker 8767
real_service.timing: One public bus image, 31 ordered frames plus a separate one-frame session per configuration. Median uses the 30 post-first frames. Fixture roundtrip excludes camera/encoding; no GPU-after control or browser FPS claim

pedestrian_light_probe.observed: Neutral pedestrian light class84, unknown state for below-threshold green score; real protocol transport only, not physical light accuracy or a performance comparison

interpretation.decision: Keep host fusion explicitly selectable and enable it in the local original-model service; retain GPU fusion as repository default
interpretation.day: Both original and walk host candidates reduce full-frame mean relative to both bracketing controls
interpretation.night: No stable universal full-frame gain: the first walk-night candidate regresses against the earlier control, while the independent replicate improves against both. Report each comparison separately
interpretation.forward: Reuse the previously validated FP32 TensorRT forward acceleration; this round reduces depth fusion overhead and does not claim a new Forward gain
interpretation.static_service: Walk bus fixture median improves about17.3%; original bus fixture improves about0.6%. These are ordered static probes, not whole-video or camera throughput
